doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: Why is there Government Fertilizer Subsidy program? The Ministry Of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries and Cooperatives (MOALF&C) is implementing Presidential directive on provision of subsidized fertilizer to all farmers in all counties to increase food production during the short rains season of 2022.

doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: Who qualifies for the subsidized fertilizer? A duly registered farmer whose details are in the register provided to National Cereals & Produce Board (NCPB) qualifies.

doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: What do I need to be able to buy subsidized fertilizer? You need to appear in person at the nearest NCPB depot with your original identity card and your name must be in the register.

doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: Can I buy subsidized fertilizer on behalf of somebody else? No, that is not acceptable.

doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: What if am not registered? You are requested to visit your County or Sub county or Ward Agricultural Office for registration.

doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: Do I need to pay for registration as a farmer? No, registration is free of charge. You only need to visit the nearest County, Sub-county or ward Agricultural Office.

doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: Where can I get the fertilizer from? You can get the subsidized fertilizer from any of the nearest NCPB depots within the county where you are registered.

doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: How many bags of fertilizer can a farmer buy? Each registered farmer is entitled to a combined maximum of loo bags for both planting and top-dressing fertilizer per season depending on the registered acreage of the land prepared for planting. A farmer is allowed two bags each for planting and top dressing per acre, e.g. • A farmer with 3 acres of land can buy up to a maximum of 12 bags • A farmer with 15 acres can buy up to 60 bags • A farmer with over 25 acres can buy up to 100 bags

doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: How much do I pay for the subsidized fertilizers? Approved subsidized fertilizer selling price per 50kg bag (Kshs.) 1. DAP 3,500 2. NPKs 3,275 3. MOP 1,775 4. UREA 3,500 5. CAN 2,875 6. Local Blends (Planting) 3,275 7. Local Blends (Top dressing) 3,275 8. Sulphate of Ammonia 2,220

doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: How do I make the payment? There are two ways of making payments at NCPB upon approval by depot manager: a) M-pesa transactions through NCPB Till Number displayed at the Depot directly from your mobile phone number. b) Bank account deposit as provided by the Depot/Silo Manager. c) Payments from Farmer cooperatives societies/organization must be made directly from their bank account directly to NCPB bank account provided by the respective depot/silo manager. Cash payments at the depot shall NOT be accepted.

doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: Can a farmer buy on credit? No, farmers are required to pay before collecting the fertilizer.

doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: Can I buy all the subsidized fertilizer I need once? No, you can buy what you need any time as long as the maximum allowed as per your acreage is not exceeded.

doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: Can one buy the fertilizer and resell to others? NO, this is ILLEGAL.

doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: Can Co-operatives and farmer organizations benefit from the program? Yes: All farmer co-operatives and other farmer’s organizations shall benefit if legally registered. Each individual co-operative member must be registered and their names must appear in the farmers register held by NCPB Depot/Silo.

doc_title: NCPB Government Subsidized Fertilizer Program — Frequently Asked Questions
text: At what time can I buy the fertilizer? All NCPB depots are open Monday to Friday from 8.00am to 5.00pm.

doc_title: CS Dr Andrew Karanja presides over the launch of the 2025 Long Rains NFSP at NCPB GPC Depot, Nairobi
publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development
text: The National Cereals and Produce Board (NCPB), a key agency continues to play a pivotal role in distributing subsidized fertilizer to farmers. Regarding past concerns regarding fertilizer quality, the CS assured Kenyans that the government has taken rigorous measures to address these issues. Every batch of fertilizer is now subjected to thorough inspection to ensure only high-quality products reach farmers, he added.

doc_title: CS Dr Andrew Karanja presides over the launch of the 2025 Long Rains NFSP at NCPB GPC Depot, Nairobi
publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development
text: The Kenya Kwanza Government remains steadfast in its commitment to ensuring food security and access to nutritious, quality food. Through this subsidy program, we have witnessed significant improvements in food production, reduced costs of basic commodities, and enhanced livelihoods for farmers.

doc_title: CS Dr Andrew Karanja presides over the launch of the 2025 Long Rains NFSP at NCPB GPC Depot, Nairobi
publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development
text: For the 2025 long rains season, the government has procured 7.4 million bags of fertilizer, the bulk of which will be delivered to stores by mid-January 2025. Distribution is set to commence at the end of January, ensuring our farmers are well-prepared by the onset of the rains in mid-March.

doc_title: CS Dr Andrew Karanja presides over the launch of the 2025 Long Rains NFSP at NCPB GPC Depot, Nairobi
publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development
text: To enhance accessibility, the government is increasing the number of outlets through partnerships with cooperatives and agro-vet stores, in addition to the existing NCPB depots.

doc_title: CS Dr Andrew Karanja presides over the launch of the 2025 Long Rains NFSP at NCPB GPC Depot, Nairobi
publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development
text: Registered farmers will receive e-vouchers, which they can redeem at these outlets. County governments remain actively involved to streamline the process and reach as many farmers as possible.

doc_title: CS Dr Andrew Karanja presides over the launch of the 2025 Long Rains NFSP at NCPB GPC Depot, Nairobi
publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development
text: The price of government subsidized fertilizer will remain at an affordable Ksh 2,500 per 50-kg bag this season, ensuring that more farmers benefit from this program.

doc_title: Streaming Distribution and Issuance of Subsidized Fertilizer Across the Country
publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development
text: Ahead of National Farmers’ day Celebration in Uasin Gishu county, the principal secretary state department for Agriculture Dr kipronoh Ronoh Paul, CBS took the time to visit the Eldoret National Cereals and Produce Board (NCPB) Depot in Soy Constituency. The purpose of his visit was to monitor Subsidized Fertilizer and certified seeds Program and explore ways to improve last mile distribution through the establishment of additional distribution stores in the county, including through farmers cooperatives.

doc_title: Streaming Distribution and Issuance of Subsidized Fertilizer Across the Country
publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development
text: At the NCPB depot, PS had a brief meeting with the management to discuss the modalities of setting up additional distribution stores with a view of enhancing the distribution of farm inputs to farmers. The subsidized fertilizer is being sold at a reduced price of Sh2,500 from the original price of Sh6,500 at either National Cereals and Produce Board (NCPB) or Kenya National Trading Corporation (KNTC) stores.

doc_title: Streaming Distribution and Issuance of Subsidized Fertilizer Across the Country
publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development
text: After the meeting with the management, he engaged with farmers present at the depot to hear their feedback on the fertilizer distribution process and address any bottlenecks they may have encountered. So far, the feedback was positive, and the distribution process will be smoothly. He was flanked by Governors Hon. Ken Lusaka, Chair of Agriculture at the Council of Governors, Hon. Jonathan Bii(Host),MPS Hon. David Kiplangat ( Soy), Hon. Phylis Bartoo (Moiben),MD Kenya seeds Company Mr Sammy Chepsiror, Hosts of MCAs among other key stakeholders.

doc_title: County Government Intensifies Last Mile Subsidised Fertiliser Distribution Ahead of Heavy Rains
text: The County Government of Kakamega has stepped up last mile subsidised fertiliser distribution in partnership with the National Cereals and Produce Board (NCPB) ahead of the heavy rains season to boost farm productivity and ensure farmers take full advantage of favourable planting conditions. Registered farmers purchase fertiliser at Ksh 2,500 per 50-kilogram bag through an E-voucher system and redeem it at designated collection centres across the county.

doc_title: County Government Intensifies Last Mile Subsidised Fertiliser Distribution Ahead of Heavy Rains
text: To ensure efficiency and accountability, trained agriculture officers have been deployed to coordinate the exercise. The fertiliser is now available at 16 county-managed collection centres, in addition to four NCPB outlets, bringing the total number of collection points to 20. Registered farmers are encouraged to collect their fertiliser at the designated collection point nearest to them.

doc_title: County Government Intensifies Last Mile Subsidised Fertiliser Distribution Ahead of Heavy Rains
text: The subsidised price was implemented following a directive by Governor FCPA Dr. Fernandes Barasa as part of efforts to reduce the cost of farm inputs and improve yields for smallholder farmers. With the ongoing rains, timely access to fertiliser is expected to increase acreage under cultivation, boost production of staple crops such as maize and beans, lower household farming costs, and improve rural livelihoods.

doc_title: County Government Intensifies Last Mile Subsidised Fertiliser Distribution Ahead of Heavy Rains
text: Additionally, the County Government has announced that free fertiliser will soon be distributed to less fortunate farmers, including widows and persons with disabilities, to promote inclusivity and ensure no household is left behind.

doc_title: County Government Intensifies Last Mile Subsidised Fertiliser Distribution Ahead of Heavy Rains
text: This programme advances Governor Barasa’s Food Security and Wealth Creation agenda, reinforcing the administration’s commitment to inclusive agricultural support and sustainable prosperity across Kakamega County.

doc_title: Government Reduces Fertilizer Price to KSh 2,000 as NCPB Delivers Subsidized Fertilizer Across Kakamega
text: Kakamega County has received subsidized fertilizer through the National Cereals & Produce Board (NCPB)last-mile delivery programme, with consignments delivered to various distribution points across the County.

doc_title: Government Reduces Fertilizer Price to KSh 2,000 as NCPB Delivers Subsidized Fertilizer Across Kakamega
text: Following the Government’s latest price reduction, farmers can now purchase the subsidized fertilizer at KSh 2,000 per 50kg bag, making farm inputs more affordable as farmers prepare for the short rains.

doc_title: Government Reduces Fertilizer Price to KSh 2,000 as NCPB Delivers Subsidized Fertilizer Across Kakamega
text: The initiative is part of the efforts by H.E. Governor Fernandes Barasa to support farmers, boost agricultural production, and strengthen food security across Kakamega County.

doc_title: Government Reduces Fertilizer Price to KSh 2,000 as NCPB Delivers Subsidized Fertilizer Across Kakamega
text: A total of 16 stores have been identified as fertilizer distribution points across the County, bringing subsidized farm inputs closer to farmers.

doc_title: Farmers assured of steady subsidised fertiliser supply (Machakos)
text: The Government through the Ministry of Agriculture, has assured farmers in the lower Eastern Regions of Machakos, Kitui and Makueni counties of the availability of enough subsidised fertiliser at the four allocated depots in Machakos.

doc_title: Farmers assured of steady subsidised fertiliser supply (Machakos)
text: Secretary Administration in State Department for Agriculture Rashid Khator, while speaking at the Machakos National Cereals Produce Board (NCPB), said that farmers are encouraged to continue redeeming and collecting fertiliser for their farms.

doc_title: Farmers assured of steady subsidised fertiliser supply (Machakos)
text: Khator, who also chairs the National Fertiliser Technical Committee, added that farmers should take advantage of the rains to collect fertiliser suitable for their farms and increase their food production.

doc_title: Farmers assured of steady subsidised fertiliser supply (Machakos)
text: “We are encouraging farmers to continue collecting fertiliser which are available at all depots so that when the rains settle, they can make use of the fertiliser as we increase its production for different value chains,” said Rashid.

doc_title: Farmers assured of steady subsidised fertiliser supply (Machakos)
text: On fears of substandard fertiliser, he confirmed that the government has put systems in place to ensure fertiliser is checked before it arrives at the Mombasa port and before it’s distributed to the depots.

doc_title: Farmers assured of steady subsidised fertiliser supply (Machakos)
text: He added that if there are any complaints about the quality of the fertiliser, then one is free to report and share their issues at the nearest depot.

doc_title: Farmers assured of steady subsidised fertiliser supply (Machakos)
text: Salim Jacob, a farmer from Mitaboni in Machakos, on his part, said that he has been using the subsidised fertiliser for his maize for a long time and has enjoyed quality yields.

doc_title: Farmers assured of steady subsidised fertiliser supply (Machakos)
text: Salim appreciated the government’s efforts in providing farmers with suitable fertilisers.

doc_title: Farmers assured of steady subsidised fertiliser supply (Machakos)
text: He added that at the depot, he was advised to use the DH04 type of fertiliser, which has helped him achieve a good yield.

doc_title: Farmers assured of steady subsidised fertiliser supply (Machakos)
text: “I encourage farmers from Ukambani to come for fertiliser at the Machakos NCPB, where there are plenty and where one will be advised on the proper usage of different types of fertilisers for their farms,” added Salim.

doc_title: State Unveils e-Voucher System
text: The Government has finalized plans to roll out a digital platform through which at least 200, 000 small scale farmers can enlist for supply of farm inputs at affordable rates.

doc_title: State Unveils e-Voucher System
text: The National e-voucher program and the ministry’s digital strategy are set to be launched this Friday by the Agriculture cabinet secretary, Peter Munya at the Ahero Multipurpose Centre in Kisumu County.

doc_title: State Unveils e-Voucher System
text: Agriculture PS Hamadi Boga told a virtual press briefing ahead of the launch of the Evoucher Digital Programme that farmers in 12 selected pilot counties will benefit from the new system which was tailored to improve food production in the country.

doc_title: State Unveils e-Voucher System
text: He insisted that only registered farmers were eligible for the voucher to be issued by respective county government to facilitate them access seeds, fertilizer, agrochemicals and insurance from authorized agro-dealers.

doc_title: State Unveils e-Voucher System
text: Boga said the new approach commonly known as the e-voucher program falls under the National Value Chain Support Program intends to empower small scale farmers produce more and facilitate efforts to make the country food secure.

doc_title: State Unveils e-Voucher System
text: “Under the evoucher system, farmers will receive a voucher from their respective County Governments to buy farm inputs from the nearest agrodealers, who will later claim their payments from the government” he explained.

doc_title: State Unveils e-Voucher System
text: The PS said the program was part of the government’s digital agenda that was designed to improve the fertilizer subsidy program adding that at least 1.4 million farmers were targeted by the year 2023 and at least 2,300 agro-dealers will be involved in the provision of the farm inputs to the tune of Ksh 0.7 billion.

doc_title: State Unveils e-Voucher System
text: Boga underscored the critical role data and digital solutions played in agricultural production and the general livelihood and income of farmers as such information enabled them planned ahead to avert losses.

doc_title: State Unveils e-Voucher System
text: He said another point of focus was to unlock the over 500,000 acres of agricultural production land that was underutilized and encouraging farmers invest in agro-processing venture to improve the value chains..

doc_title: State Unveils e-Voucher System
text: “By upscaling and expanding its reach for better impact, whilst building on regional and local experiences and lessons learned. The e-voucher program will support agricultural production and marketing through input-subsidized agriculture using an electronic voucher input management system. This will be achieved through input subsidy support & incentives including seeds, agrochemicals, extension services and, later, insurance and market-linkages,” he said.

doc_title: State Unveils e-Voucher System
text: In 2008, the government started the subsidized fertilizer program to caution farmers against high prices of fertiliser and also help in improving productivity. But over the years, unscrupulous traders colluded with officials at the National Cereals and Produce Board to buy the subsidy fertiliser, and could repackage it and then sell back to farmers at a higher price.

doc_title: State Unveils e-Voucher System
text: The launch comes after the government in November 2018 proposed to use e-vouchers for farmers to buy subsidized fertilizer from private agro-vet shops, to weed out unscrupulous traders who had infiltrated the distribution chain to cash on the bureaucratic process at the time.

doc_title: State Unveils e-Voucher System
text: Timothy Njagi, a researcher from Tegemeo Institute of Agricultural Policy and Development- Egerton University expressed feras that the fertilizer subsidy program should be redesigned to make more impact to farmers and increase productivity.
